title: New Jersey's 10th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat LaMonica McIver against Republican challenger Carmen Bucco. This heavily Democratic district — with a 54% Democratic voter registration advantage over just 10% Republican — covers parts of Essex, Union, and Hudson counties, including Newark, East Orange, Irvington, and parts of Jersey City. McIver, first elected in a September 2024 special election following the death of Rep. Donald Payne Jr., won renomination in the June 2 Democratic primary. Bucco, a perennial candidate and small business owner, ran unopposed in the Republican primary. The race is a rematch of the 2024 general election, which McIver won by a wide margin in this safe Democratic seat.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically for the 2026 New Jersey 10th Congressional District general election as of mid-June 2026. The district is considered a safe Democratic seat and has not been the subject of independent polling this cycle.

candidates.name: LaMonica McIver
candidates.summary: LaMonica McIver is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District, first elected in a September 2024 special election. She previously served as Newark Municipal Council President and is the first Black woman and youngest person ever elected to Congress from New Jersey. McIver advocates for economic equity, universal healthcare, comprehensive immigration reform, and environmental justice; she was charged in June 2025 with impeding federal officers during a congressional oversight visit at an immigration detention facility.

candidates.name: Carmen Bucco
candidates.summary: Carmen Bucco is a Republican small business owner from Kenilworth who is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District. A product of the foster care system who experienced homelessness as a youth, Bucco founded Bucco's Rising Stars Foundation and has been active in Republican politics for over 20 years. He is a former elected member of the Belleville Board of Education and has run unsuccessfully for several offices including State Senate, Commissioner, and Congress in 2024. Bucco campaigns on public safety, anti-corruption, immigration enforcement, and local control of issues such as abortion.

forecast.rationale: No public district-specific polls exist for the 2026 NJ-10 race, limiting confidence. However, the structural fundamentals are overwhelmingly Democratic: the district has a 54% Democratic voter registration advantage versus just 10% Republican, covering heavily Democratic urban areas (Newark, East Orange, Irvington, parts of Jersey City). Incumbent Democrat LaMonica McIver already won the seat in a 2024 special election and the 2024 general election by wide margins. Challenger Carmen Bucco is a perennial Republican candidate who has lost multiple prior races for various offices and ran unopposed in the primary, demonstrating minimal party investment. Given the massive registration gap, incumbency advantage, and lack of any polling suggesting competitiveness, a Democratic hold is all but certain.
